summary.plain: A gamma-ray observatory on a Mexican volcano: an array of water tanks 4100 metres up that watches nearly the whole sky at once for the highest-energy light in the universe, day and night.
summary.technical: Water-Cherenkov gamma-ray/cosmic-ray air-shower array at 4100 m on Sierra Negra, Mexico, with a wide (~2 sr) instantaneous field of view sensitive up to 100 TeV. Under construction as of September 2013, taking partial-array data from November 2014, full-array operations from March 2015.

unique_capabilities.quote: up to 100 TeV... nearly 2 sr at any instant
unique_capabilities.value: A wide field-of-view (nearly 2 steradian instantaneous), continuously operating ground array that surveys the gamma-ray sky at TeV-PeV energies without pointing, unlike imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes.
